Monster Hunter: World is my first entry into the series, and from what little I heard about the gameplay loop (hunt monster -> upgrade gear with monster -> hunt new monster and repeat), I was worried I'd quickly get bored of the game after hunting the first few monsters.

However, after trying out all the unique weapons and hunting the first few monsters encountered in the game, I found myself enjoying it way more than I expected. I realized that there was more to Monster Hunter than the core gameplay loop. All of the monsters were unique in their design and abilities, so I always looked forward to the next monster encounter. Furthermore, all of the weapons played very differently from each other and have a high skill ceiling which encouraged me to learn how to fight more efficiently with my main weapon while keeping the gameplay fresh by playing with weapons I'm not familiar with.

Overall I highly recommend Monster Hunter: World if you're looking for an immersive RPG with a deep combat system, and if you find yourself wanting more, I recommend buying the Iceborne expansion as its additional content more than doubles the content from the base game and the technical issues with save files being lost during the initial release of Iceborne has since been fixed.

I was recommended Monster Hunter: World by a friend, and bought this game a few months ago. Little did I know at the time, that I would gradually get hooked.

At first I felt overwhelmed, because not only is this my first time getting into the series, there is a lot to learn as the start of the game throws a lot of information at you. Of course it's not all intruding, so you can play the game at your own pace. The learning curve is quite huge (especially for new players to the series), sooner or later you'll probably realise that there just isn't enough explanations for everything and one may find themself looking up guides and videos frequently.
There are plenty of weapons to choose from (14 in fact) and they all have their own unique combat style/techniques. Monster variety for you to slay/capture is also plentiful, so you'll always have something to pick a fight with. Playing the game solo is pretty fun, but I think battling monsters with other people brings out a lot more excitement, so if you have friends, do invite them to tag along!

(Currently there is a partial fix though f you go to steam/steamapps/common/monster hunter world/ open the config file there's a setting that says MouseBaseSpeed=2.000000. Change this number so that max feels quicker Example number .2)

This is the kind of game that I don't play alone, which means my experience is enhanced by my friends being fun to hang out with.

The game revolves around hunting monsters, if you couldn't tell by the title. By using different weapons, you run around in contained environments to find and kill or capture the monster of the day. It's a challenging experience, the monsters will not go quietly especially the more dangerous ones, but it's also rewarding. The different fighting styles are fun, and varied enough that it feels like the weapon you choose does matter.

However it's not a very convenient game. Starting up multiplayer is annoying, and random loot drops means you'll be hunting the same beast twenty times just to get that specific material you need for one weapon. You'll definitely have to get into the grind mindset if you want the best gear.

The story is alright, it's not what I remember of the game but it doesn't intrude. Unlike some side characters who tended to get on my nerves constantly.

All in all I've had a lot of fun with this game, and you might too.
